title: My first prototype vs today: I'd never opened Unity — 6 months later my game is live on CrazyGames
author: porroypapitas
selftext:
I come from design and animation — Photoshop and After Effects my whole career, no coding. On April 4 I connected Claude to Unity through MCP for the first time.

What made it work wasn't a magic prompt: I knew exactly how I wanted the game to feel from a lifetime of playing, and I iterated a lot. Halfway through I took a Git + Unity course and learned from a senior dev, which changed how I worked with the AI.

The result: Cuetazos, an arcade tank brawler for up to 4 players on one screen. Art, code and music made with AI tools, directed and iterated by me.

What actually made the difference: giving the AI a written memory of every decision (one doc per game area), Git with one branch per task so I could roll back when it broke something, and playtesting with friends every week — the AI can't tell you something isn't fun.

Free on CrazyGames (PC): [https://www.crazygames.com/game/cuetazos-wtn](https://www.crazygames.com/game/cuetazos-wtn)

Happy to answer anything about the workflow.

comments.author: sOCkmONke
comments.body:
Hey thanks for sharing!

Question on process coming from a creative industry already. Did you implement art/character review process with notes and modifications? Or was it more adhoc waterfall through playtesting?

replies.author: porroypapitas
replies.body:
Hi! thanks you!  
Bit of both. I'm solo, so no formal notes rounds but for each character piece I make 3 concepts painted over real in-game screenshots, pick one and iterate before producing the final asset. After that playtesting drives the tweaks mostly readability and scale.

replies.author: sOCkmONke
replies.body:
Cool! The real in game paint overs are a great process step that still works with AI tools. I maybe have a similar back ground, i was in game dev and now solo process with AI tools. One artifact working with claude was great for review that maybe you could use for reviewing animations for readability.

Assets aren’t great, but hopefully you get the gist.   
https://claude.ai/artifact/MFGMTY3Y5EFk1taeqhgiBY

replies.author: porroypapitas
replies.body: That's a really smart use of artifacts! Reviewing animations side by side for readability is exactly where I lose the most time especially with VFX at small scale on screen. I'll definitely try something like that. Thanks for sharing!
